what_its_for: Estramustine is a cancer medicine used to treat prostate cancer that has spread or gotten worse. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_to_take: Take estramustine capsules by mouth with a full glass of water. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. Do not take it with milk, dairy products, or calcium-rich foods and drinks, as these can make the medicine less effective. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. Try to take it at the same times each day.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body weight and health condition. The usual dose is taken 3 times a day. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own. Take all doses exactly as prescribed, even if you feel well.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store estramustine capsules in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from children and pets. Do not freeze. Do not store in the bathroom, where heat and moisture can damage the medicine. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating or drinking milk, cheese, yogurt, ice cream, or other dairy products within 1 to 2 hours of taking your dose, as calcium can block the medicine from working properly. Avoid taking antacids or calcium supplements at the same time as this medicine. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase side effects. Do not get vaccines (especially live vaccines) without checking with your doctor first. Use effective birth control — estramustine can harm an unborn baby. Do not father a child while taking this medicine and for some time after stopping.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing up blood (possible blood clot); severe leg pain or swelling; signs of a stroke such as sudden numbness, weakness, confusion, vision changes, or trouble speaking; signs of heart attack such as chest tightness or pain spreading to your arm or jaw; severe allergic reaction including rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat; or any new or worsening symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: Estramustine does not cure prostate cancer, but it helps to slow its growth and spread. It may take several weeks before you notice improvement. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and check-ups. Continue taking the medicine as directed even if you do not feel immediate changes — stopping it suddenly can be harmful.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially blood clots and heart problems. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as this medicine may need to be used with extra caution or avoided. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is for men only and must not be used by women who are pregnant or breastfeeding. Men taking this medicine should use effective birth control to prevent pregnancy in their partner. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
